_readme: The goddess who brought Sam over (js/logic/goddess.js, docs/GODDESS.md). Numbers are in balance.json → goddess.
Placeholders: {goddess} her name, {sam}, {house}, {partner} (first name), {past} (Sam's past life, lowercase), {lady} (a lady's first name), {n}, {names}, {cycle}, {skill}.
Any text field may be a list: one entry is picked at random.

rebirth: at every New Game+ before the binding. fast/steady/slow = how quickly he paid (weeks vs the plan). lovers/alone = lovers carried or none. jealous.low/mid/high by her jealousy. bound.low/mid/high = after the binding, by her divinity.

teases: her scenes before the binding, picked by evGoddess: story scenes (non-repeat) play in file order, each once, from minCycle on; maxCycle is only when they're due, a missed one stays available and makes her visit more often (balance.json → goddess.events.catchUp). Repeat scenes are filler, gated by minCycle-maxCycle, and only show once every unlocked story scene has been seen. Fields: id, title, text, choices [{label, res, love, jealousy, energy (Sam's), reveal}], minCycle, maxCycle, form ('disguise' = random non-true form, 'true' = her own form, or a form key), repeat (filler, may recur, never marked seen), unknown (only before Sam has worked it out), needKnows (only after), reveal (taking the event, or a choice with reveal, sets g.knows), image {comp, setting, sam, pov} (comp describes pose/scene only: the code adds her look). Placeholders: {alias} the name she gives in this form, {form} e.g. 'a fox-eared girl', {race}, {goddess} (only when he knows / true form). Phases: stranger (cycles 1-2, st_*), suspicion (2-3, su_*), reveal (3), game (3-5, gm_*, after the reveal) and true-form scenes (3-5, tr_* and inside/almost/question). She never lets Sam finish: that would bind her.
remarks.low/mid/high: short jealous remarks (by jealousy) as weekly events, from cycle `remarksFrom` (3) on; remarkChoices are their default answers.

binding: the first rebirth after a lady has lived a fully reincarnated life; she confesses it was never a whim. focus: her weekly guidance options (report lines; indulge has feminine/futa variants, chosen by her form setting). claim: what she does when jealousy wins. night: Sam's action on her tab (image, open by divinity low/mid/high, then inside / outside / unhappy lists by how the night ended; {act} = the service label, lowercase). ending.stay/leave: full divinity again.

intro: cycle 1, before the Vane welcome. Her remarks about houses, partners and Sam's past lives live with them: economy.json → houses[id].goddess, pasts[k].goddess {intro, again}; characters.json → partner.goddess {hand, comment}. Her lines with the ladies are services.json → pair.fem/futa; on nights with Sam she uses the usual private-time lines (flavor.json → private_act).
neglect: report lines when Sam stays away (balance.json → goddess.neglect).

look: what never changes, so she's always recognizable: hairStyle, hair, eyes, skin, signature, outfit. forms[key]: one per race and beastkin sub (race, sub, build, body; label for the tab; alias = the name she gives when disguised; desc = how Sam first sees her). trueForm = her own form (story scenes, rebirths). Each form has its own image id (npc_goddess_<key>), so pictures are saved per form.

distract: what happens when a disguise tease turns into her 'distracting' Sam (goddess.js evGoddessDistract, a second event page with a samact:<service> picture at the tease's setting). lead[phase] (stranger/suspicion/reveal/game) leads in; acts[service] is what she does (falls back to flavor.json private_act); dry[tier] is how she leaves him (1 = kisses: just wanting more; 2-3 = high and dry); button[tier] is the button before the ending. Teases and their choices may set lead / dry / act (service id or list) / distract (true/false) to override. Expanded teases: intro (her arrival, its own page, button introBtn) and wonder (Sam's thoughts, shown with the choices); text is the fallback for old one-page scenes. A choice can only end in a distraction if it has resIn (what happens right before, she hasn't vanished yet; res stays the ending without one) or distract: true; then the phase chance (balance.json → goddess.tease.chance) or the tease's distract decides.

title: the Lamplighter

intro.title: Before the truck stops ringing

image.comp: a radiant goddess with a glowing bronze skin and a small ember-flame at her shoulder, sitting in a dark void lit by hundreds of hanging paper lanterns, looking down with an amused smile, one hand extended
image.setting: an endless dark space full of floating paper lanterns

intro.open:
The horn is still ringing when the dark fills up with lanterns. Hundreds of them, hanging from nothing.

A woman sits among them as if on a swing, barefoot, a little ember-flame drifting lazily around her shoulder. Her skin glows from within like a lantern, gold markings brightening at her collarbones and hips as she looks Sam over, slowly, head to toe, like someone deciding what to unwrap first.

"Sam Takahashi. Thirty-one years of being nice to people and nobody ever once being nice back on purpose." She tilts her head. "I'm {goddess}. I light the way across, for the ones I pick. I picked you. On a whim, mostly. Don't read into it." She smiles like a woman who is reading into it a great deal.
intro.close:
"There's a debt. There's always a debt, it keeps you honest. Pay it, and if you're still interesting, I'll bring you back and we'll do it again." She trails one fingertip down his chest, leans close enough that her warmth fills the dark, and doesn't kiss him. "I'll be watching. Everything. Give me something worth watching."

The lanterns go out, one by one.

When he wakes, the lanterns slip away like a dream, and by the time he's tying his shoes there is only a warm smell of candle smoke, and a faint feeling of having forgotten something that mattered.

rebirth.title: Again, {sam}?

image.comp: a radiant goddess with glowing bronze skin and a small ember-flame at her shoulder, lounging on a crescent of lantern-light, chin on her hand, smiling down, dress slipping off one shoulder
image.setting: an endless dark space full of floating paper lanterns

open:
The lanterns again. {goddess} is lying on her stomach across a crescent of light, chin in her hands, feet kicking idly, her dress slipping off one shoulder and no effort made to fix it.

"Debt paid. Look at you." She looks him over, unhurried. "Come here and let me see what the work did to you."

Darkness, then the warm smell of candle smoke. {goddess} is waiting, sitting on nothing, legs crossed, the little ember-flame circling her shoulder like a pet. "There he is. My favorite investment." She crooks a finger.

"Welcome back." {goddess} doesn't look up from the lantern she's turning in her hands. Inside it, very small, is the house he just left. "You did it again. I watched all of it. All of it, {sam}. You have no idea how much I enjoyed some of those nights."
fast: "That was quick. Show-off." She sounds pleased anyway. "I do like a man who gets the job done."
"Paid early. Marguerite nearly smiled, did you see? I had money on it. Now you owe me a kiss."
steady: "Right on schedule. Reliable. It's a good look on you." Her eyes drift down and back up. "Mostly."
"Not fast, not slow. You're very consistent, {sam}. I like a man with stamina."
slow: "That went right down to the wire. I had to watch through my fingers." She doesn't say which fingers she was using.
"You cut that close. Do you know how boring the afterlife paperwork is? Don't make me do it. I'd rather be doing you." She doesn't even pretend to have misspoken.
lovers: "And you're taking {names} with you." A pause that lasts slightly too long. "Of course you are. I hope they appreciate what I've been doing to keep you in such good shape."
"{names}. Again." She counts on her fingers and stops before she runs out. "Sweet. Do tell me everything later."
alone: "Nobody coming along this time? Hm." She looks like she wants to be disappointed for you and can't quite manage it. "More of you for me, then."

low: "Go on, then. Have fun. Tell me about it after."
"Enjoy yourself." A smile. "I will be, vicariously."
mid: "There are a lot of them now, {sam}." She says it lightly. She's looking at the lanterns, not at him.
"You know they don't remember me? Only you do. I find that very fair. Mostly."
high: She catches his chin before he goes and holds it, thumb against his lip. "Every life, more of them. I brought you here. Remember that."
"I counted them. I didn't mean to. I count everything I'm not allowed to have." Her hand slides down his chest, and lingers.

close:
She kisses two fingers and presses them to his forehead, then, after a thought, to his mouth. The lanterns go out.

When he wakes, the lanterns are already fading like a dream, and he can't quite remember whose face was looking down at him.
"Off you go." She flicks his nose, then smooths a hand down his front like she's checking the goods. The dark folds up like paper. The dream is going already; by morning it'll be gone.
"Don't keep me waiting." She almost sounds like she means something by it. Then the lanterns go out. He wakes with the taste of candle smoke and nothing else.

low: This time there are no lanterns. {goddess} is just there when he wakes, warm against his side, mortal-tired, one leg thrown over his. "Again," she mumbles into his neck. "I'm coming too. Obviously."
mid: {goddess} wakes him by pressing close, glowing brighter than last time, the little ember-flame bobbing over her shoulder. "Another life. I'm getting some of it back, you know. Mostly thanks to you. Don't let it go to your head." She kisses him to make sure it does.
high: {goddess} is already up, glowing faintly, watching him sleep with her chin on her hand. "Nearly whole again," she says when he opens his eyes, and slides closer. She doesn't say what happens then.

knows: "You remember," {goddess} says, before he's finished opening his eyes. She's grinning, and a little teary, and doesn't bother to hide either. "Each time you wake up you forget a bit less. Good. I like being known." She pulls him close by the collar. "Now come here, and let me remind you what you've been missing."

"Hello, {sam}. Don't say it, I know: you knew it was me the whole time." {goddess} is lounging across the dark, eyes half-lidded, thoroughly smug. "You're getting good at this. Go on. Go and pay your debt, and I'll find a new face to tease you with." She trails a fingertip down his chest and stops, exactly where she always stops.

teases.title: A stranger at the bar

image.comp: a girl sitting very close to a man at a bar counter, her hand on his thigh, leaning in to whisper in his ear, teasing smile
image.setting: the bar of a lantern-lit pleasure house at night

teases.text:
The girl at the end of the bar isn't a guest and isn't staff, and she's been watching Sam over the rim of her glass for ten minutes. {form}, very long black hair, gold at the tips, eyes that catch the lamplight a little too well.

"{alias}," she says, when he finally goes over, as if he'd asked. "You're the owner. You look like you haven't sat down since the morning." She hooks a foot around his stool and pulls it closer. "Sit. Let someone look after you for once."

She does, for an hour: a hand on his knee, a thumb along his jaw, a laugh against his ear. Then he looks down at his drink, and when he looks up again the stool is empty and the glass is still warm.

choices.label: "Have we met?"
choices.resIn: "Mm. Have we?" She tilts her head, considering him, and something in her eyes looks almost pleased that he asked.
choices.res: "Not yet," she says, and taps his nose. He looks down at his drink for one heartbeat, and when he looks up the stool is empty and her glass is still warm. He checks the hall, the stairs, the street. Nobody.

choices.label: Enjoy it while it lasts
choices.resIn: He stops trying to work her out and lets the noise of the bar fade. She notices, and her smile turns slow and very warm.
choices.res: He lets her talk, and lets her hand wander, and for an hour this world feels kind. Then he blinks, and she's gone, and the stool beside him is empty. A lucky night, wasted. He tells himself these things happen. In this world, apparently, they do.

teases.intro:
The bar is loud tonight, which is good for business and bad for Sam's head. He's been on his feet since dawn: ledgers, a broken shutter, a client who wanted a refund for reasons he declined to explain.

The girl at the end of the counter isn't a guest and isn't staff. She's been there for ten minutes with one untouched glass, watching him over the rim of it. {form}, with very long black hair that turns to gold at the tips, and eyes that catch the lamplight a little too well.

When he finally goes over to ask if she needs anything, she answers before he can. "{alias}." As if he'd asked. "You're the owner. You look like you haven't sat down since this morning." She hooks a foot around the stool beside her and drags it closer. "Sit. Let someone look after you for once."
teases.wonder:
He sits. He isn't sure why. She talks about nothing (the weather, the music, the terrible painting over the door) and her hand settles on his knee as if it's always lived there.

Sam tries to place her. Not one of his ladies. Not a client's companion; she came alone. Not anyone from the street, either: he would remember hair like that, the way the gold at the ends seems to glow a little in the dark corners of the room. There's something familiar about her laugh, though, like a song he heard once in a dream and can't quite hum.

Her thumb traces his jaw. "You're thinking very hard," {alias} says. "About me?"

teases.title: A visitor in the night

image.comp: a girl sitting on the edge of a man's bed at night leaning in for a kiss, her hand under the blanket, candle-light

teases.text:
Sam wakes because the room is warm. Someone is sitting on the edge of his bed: {form}, black hair spilling over her shoulders, gold tips glowing faintly in the dark.

"Shh. I'm {alias}. You didn't hear me come in." She leans down and kisses him, slow and very thorough, one hand sliding under the blanket to rest on his stomach. He's too startled to do anything but kiss back. Her hand drifts lower. Lower. And the bed is empty, the door is shut and locked, and the room is cold.

choices.label: Kiss her back
choices.res: He catches the last of it before she's gone, and lies awake for an hour, aching. Somewhere far off, someone laughs, pleased.
choices.resIn: He opens his mouth to say something, anything, and she catches the words before they leave, with a kiss that is slow and unhurried and entirely sure of itself. The blanket slides lower.

choices.label: "Who are you?"
choices.res: "Someone who likes you," says the dark, amused, from nowhere. "Goodnight, {sam}."
choices.resIn: "Who are you?" She seems to find the question adorable. "Someone who couldn't sleep," she murmurs, and her mouth finds his before he can ask a second one, her hand wandering down under the blanket.

teases.intro:
The house has gone quiet the way it only does after the last guest is out and the last lantern is trimmed. Sam has been asleep for an hour, face down, one arm hanging off the mattress, dreaming about spreadsheets.

What wakes him is the warmth. Not the blanket kind: the kind that has a weight to it, sitting on the edge of the bed and making the mattress dip. Candle smoke, faint and sweet, as if someone had just walked in from a room full of them.

{form} is sitting there in the dark, black hair spilling over her shoulders so long it pools on the sheets, the tips glowing a soft gold. Her eyes are the color of lamplight. "Shh," she says, before he can get a word out. "I'm {alias}. You didn't hear me come in."
teases.wonder:
Sam is almost sure this is a dream. The door was locked; he locked it himself. The window is two floors up. And yet there is a very solid, very warm person on his bed, and her hand is resting on his stomach through the blanket as if she'd been invited.

He doesn't know her. He is certain he doesn't know her. So why does the shape of her smile feel like a word on the tip of his tongue? Why does the smoke in the air remind him of somewhere high and golden, with paper lanterns swaying in a warm wind?

She leans closer, her hair sliding across his chest like cool silk, and waits to see what he'll do with the moment.

teases.title: Between the shelves

image.comp: a girl pressing a man back against shelves in a dim storeroom, kissing his neck, her hand at his belt

teases.text:
Sam is fetching linens from the storeroom when the door clicks shut behind him. {alias}, {form}, is leaning against it with her arms behind her back, looking him over like a shopkeeper's window.

"You work too hard." She pushes him back against the shelves and presses against him, warm and close, her mouth at his throat, her hand finding his belt. "Let me help."

He's gasping, nearly there, when a knock sounds outside. "Sam? Are you in there?" He turns his head. When he turns back, the storeroom is empty, and the door is open a crack.

choices.label: Follow her out
choices.res: The hall is empty. A single gold hair is caught on his collar. He picks it off and stares at it for a while.
choices.resIn: "Wait, that door was locked from the inside." She smiles, as though he's said something sweet, and slides closer, deaf to the logistics.

choices.label: Stay and collect himself
choices.res: It takes a while. The blushing lasts longer. A strange girl, a locked door and a convenient knock. This place is wild.
choices.resIn: He doesn't say no. He doesn't say anything, and {alias} takes the silence as the yes it is, her fingers curling in the front of his shirt.

teases.intro:
The linen storeroom is the one place in the house that is always quiet, which is why Sam goes there when he needs to think. Today he needs towels, and three minutes where nobody asks him anything.

He has an armful of folded sheets when the door clicks shut behind him. He turns. {form} is leaning against it with her hands behind her back, in the dusty gold light from the one high window, looking him over the way a person looks over a shop display they've already decided to buy.

Her hair is black and ridiculously long, the tips glowing like embers. Her skin is bronze, her eyes lamp-bright. "You work too hard," she says, as if they'd been talking all morning. "{alias}. Put those down."
teases.wonder:
He puts them down. He has no idea why; his hands just do it. Maybe because no one has looked at him like that in a very long time, or maybe because she smells of candle smoke and warm skin and his brain has stopped taking orders.

He has been through every face in this house. Staff, guests, suppliers, the woman who sells lamp oil on the corner. She isn't any of them. And yet when she steps off the door and comes toward him, unhurried, there's a feeling in his chest like recognizing a handwriting.

She lays a hand flat on his chest, pushing him gently back until the shelves meet his shoulders. "Well?" she says, tilting her head. "Do you want me to stop?"

teases.title: Hot water

image.comp: a girl sitting behind a man in a steaming bath, her arms around his chest, teasing smile, steam
image.setting: a steaming wooden bath at night, lanterns

teases.text:
The bath is already hot when Sam gets in, and already occupied. {alias} settles in behind him, wraps both arms around his chest and hooks her chin over his shoulder. She's {form}, and there is nothing at all between her skin and his back.

"Breathe," she murmurs, hands wandering. They know exactly where they're going, and exactly when to stop. "That's all you get tonight."

He turns his head to answer and the water is just water, rippling gently around him, and the steam smells faintly of candle smoke.

choices.label: Lean back into her
choices.res: He leans into nothing, and the water holds him warm and still. He comes out of it oddly rested, and extremely frustrated.
choices.resIn: He lets his head fall back against her shoulder. "Breathe," she says, and her hands begin to travel.

choices.label: Turn around
choices.res: He turns around fast enough to splash. No one. A ripple of laughter lingers somewhere near the ceiling.
choices.resIn: He starts to turn, and a hand on his cheek gently stops him. "Not yet. Eyes on the water, {sam}." And he finds he doesn't mind obeying.

teases.intro:
The bathhouse at the back of the property is Sam's one luxury, a deep tiled tub fed by a hot spring that somebody before him had the good sense to build over. He gets in at the end of the longest day of the week with a groan that would embarrass him in front of staff.

The water is perfect. The steam is thick. For a full minute he just floats there with his eyes closed, listening to the lanterns tick as they cool.

Then the water moves. Not much: a ripple behind him, a soft sound of someone settling. When he opens his eyes, a pair of bronze arms slide around his chest from behind and a chin hooks over his shoulder. {form}, black hair floating around them both like ink in the water, gold at the ends. "Don't turn around," says {alias}, warm against his ear. "I'm shy."
teases.wonder:
She is clearly not shy. Sam knows this the way you know the water is wet. But it's hard to argue with her when her hands are drifting over his shoulders, working out knots he didn't know he had.

Who gets into a bath with a man they've never met? Who knows exactly where he carries the tension, and exactly how hard to press? The steam smells of candle smoke, which is strange, because the bath lamps burn lamp oil. Strange, and faintly familiar, in the way of a smell from a childhood he never had.

Her lips brush the back of his neck. "You're thinking again," she says. "I can hear it. Do you want me to make it stop?"

teases.title: The long way home

image.comp: a girl pushing a man against an alley wall, kissing him, her thigh between his, her hand inside his shirt
image.setting: a lantern-lit back alley at dusk

teases.text:
Sam is walking back from the market when a hand takes his wrist and pulls him into an alley. {alias}, {form}, pushes him against the wall with a grin and kisses him until his knees go. Her thigh slips between his; her fingers are inside his shirt.

"Do you always walk home alone?" she whispers. "Someone should do something about that." Her hand moves, and moves, and he's almost, almost, almost-

Then a cart rattles past the mouth of the alley, and when it's gone he's standing there alone, breathless, with his shirt untucked and the faint sense that he's been teased on purpose.

choices.label: Chase after her
choices.res: Nobody in the alley, nobody in the street. He walks home with his coat held in front of him.
choices.resIn: He tries to say he has errands, and she kisses the word right out of his mouth. The parcels can wait.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.res: This world runs on strange luck. The kind that gets you kissed in an alley and then leaves you shaking. He's not sure whether that's good or bad luck.
choices.resIn: He laughs, a little helplessly, because what else do you do, and the sound seems to please her. "Good," she says. "Stay right there."

teases.intro:
The market has been a long, loud errand: oil, linen, a haggle over soap that he lost on principle. Sam is cutting through the narrow lane behind the dyers' street, arms full of parcels, when the light goes strange.

A hand closes on his wrist. A very warm hand, with firm fingers. Before he has time to protest, the parcels are on the cobbles and his back is against the cool brick of an alley wall, and {form} is smiling up at him from very close.

Her hair falls to her knees, black as a night sky and tipped with gold that shines faintly even in the shade. Her eyes are the color of lamplight on honey. "Do you always walk home alone?" she asks. "{alias}. Hello."
teases.wonder:
There is a cart rattling somewhere beyond the mouth of the alley. A man is shouting about fish. The world carries on at the edge of his hearing, and none of it seems to have anything to do with the woman who has him by the collar.

Sam, who has been in this world a short while and has already been pickpocketed twice, should be checking his purse. Instead he's trying to remember where he's seen that exact shade of gold. In a dream, perhaps. Or lanterns, lots of them, floating up into a warm dark.

Her knee shifts lightly against his. "You haven't said a word," {alias} observes, delighted with herself. "Should I be worried?"

teases.title: A stranger sits down
teases.text: A girl sits down next to Sam, uninvited: {form}, with very long black hair and gold-tipped ends. "{alias}," she says, and holds out a hand he doesn't get to shake. She lays it on his thigh instead, and talks about nothing for ten minutes while her fingers draw slow patterns higher and higher. Then she excuses herself to 'fix her hair', and doesn't come back.

choices.label: Ask what she wants
choices.res: She laughs and drops the topic, her fingers sliding off his knee. Whoever she was, she's not there when he looks again, only a cooling chair and a faint smell of smoke. He goes back to work grinning like a fool.
choices.resIn: "What I want?" She seems to enjoy the question. "Hold still and I'll show you," she says, and leans in until all he can see are her eyes.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.res: He finishes the tea, and after a while realizes it is the only warm thing left at the table. He doesn't mention to anyone why his face is red.
choices.resIn: He says nothing, and she hums approvingly, her hand traveling slowly, and with great confidence, higher.

teases.intro:
It is a slow afternoon, and Sam has sat down at the corner table to let his tea go cold. He doesn't see her arrive. One moment the chair beside him is empty; the next, {form} is in it, as if she'd been there all along.

Very long black hair, gold at the tips. Eyes like lamplight. A trace of candle smoke. "{alias}," she says, and holds out a hand. When he reaches for it she lays it on his thigh instead.
teases.wonder:
Again. The thought comes before the word does. He has no reason to think "again", because he has never met this girl. And yet something inside him shrugs and says: of course.

Her fingers are drawing slow patterns on his knee while she talks about nothing in particular. He should probably say something. He's just not sure what question to ask first.

teases.title: A wink in the crowd
teases.text: In the middle of a busy evening, {alias} is just there: {form}, hip against the counter beside Sam, slipping one hand into his pocket and out again with a coin he hadn't known he had. "Tip," she says. She tucks it into his collar, brushes her lips against his ear, and her hand lingers at his waist just a moment too long. By the time the crowd shifts she has gone.

choices.label: Ask her name again
choices.res: He turns to ask and the space beside him is just space. The coin is warm against his collarbone. It is also gold, and by morning it is gone.
choices.resIn: "{alias}," she repeats, amused, and her fingers find the hem of his shirt under the counter's edge. "Pay attention."

choices.label: Play along
choices.res: The crowd shifts, someone shouts for a refill, and when he looks again she is gone. He spends the rest of the shift touching his collar.
choices.resIn: He pockets his embarrassment and leans into her. She smiles against his jaw, and the noise of the room seems to retreat a step.

teases.intro:
The evening rush is in full cry, glasses and laughter and a lute somewhere in the back, and Sam is wedged against the counter checking tabs. A hip bumps his, unhurried, and {form} is simply there beside him.

Hair so long it nearly touches the floor, black with burning gold tips. Her skin is bronze, her eyes a bright lamp-gold. She holds up a coin between two fingers. "Found this in your pocket," says {alias}. "I thought you'd like it back."
teases.wonder:
He didn't know he had a coin in that pocket. He didn't know a stranger could reach into it so gracefully. He's not even sure when she crossed the room.

She tucks the coin into his collar and presses close, with the whole crowd packed around them and no one so much as glancing over. Her breath is warm against his ear, and the smell of candle smoke lingers like a hand on the back of his neck.

teases.title: Someone is watching
teases.text:
The back stairs are dim, and someone is waiting at the top of them: {form}, long black hair, gold tips, lit from within. {alias} takes the lapels of his coat and walks him backward into the wall, kissing him with a hunger he can feel in his spine. Her knee presses. His breath breaks.

"Later," she promises, and slips out of his hands like smoke.

choices.label: Ask what she's doing
choices.res: "Later," she promises, and the shadows swallow her. The lamp has burned down by the time he thinks to move.
choices.resIn: "What does it look like?" She tugs him down by the collar and answers the question in her own way.

choices.label: Kiss her
choices.res: The stairs are empty, the lamp flickers, and Sam stays there for a long moment, one hand against the wall.
choices.resIn: He kisses her, because it seems like the only sensible answer, and feels her smile against his mouth.

teases.intro:
The back stairs are dim at this hour. Sam is on his way up with a lamp when he realizes someone is waiting at the top, and not one of his people. {form}, tall in the half-light, her black hair so long it brushes the steps, the gold tips lit as if from within.

"Late," says {alias}, and she doesn't say it as a complaint. She takes his lapels. He lets her.
teases.wonder:
The lamp is shaking a little in his hand. He hasn't even noticed. He's too busy trying to pin down why this feels like a continuation of something and not a beginning.

She walks him backward until the wall meets his shoulder blades and presses close, warm and certain. Smoke and honey and a slow, steady heat. Whoever she is, she isn't in a hurry.

teases.title: The same hair

image.comp: a girl perched on the corner of a desk, crossing her legs, leaning in to run a finger along a man's tie, teasing smile

teases.text:
It's {alias} again: {form}, a different girl, with a different name and a different pair of ears. Sam is at the desk when she perches on the corner of it, crossing her legs slowly, and asks how his night is going.

He's looking at her hair. Very long. Black. Gold at the tips, glowing faintly. The last girl had the same. And the one before that.

"Something wrong?" She leans in, smiling, and runs a finger along his tie. "You're staring."

choices.label: "Have we met?"
choices.res: "Haven't we all?" She taps his nose and kisses him on the corner of the mouth, and the door clicks, and she is not there. The pattern is getting hard to ignore.
choices.resIn: "Have we met?" She doesn't flinch. Her smile only deepens, and she slides off the desk and into his lap as though that were the answer.

choices.label: Say nothing, but watch her eyes
choices.res: Gold. Glowing. Exactly the same gold. She notices him noticing, and her smile grows slow and pleased. She's gone before he can ask.
choices.resIn: He says nothing and watches her eyes, and she notices him noticing, and for a beat the smile goes very still. Then it softens, and she leans close enough to kiss.

teases.intro:
It is late, the ledgers are open, and Sam is three columns from the end of the month when the lamp on his desk dims, flares, and steadies. He doesn't look up. Habit by now. Something in him already knows what's coming.

The desk creaks. {alias} has settled on the corner of it, {form}, a different girl with a different name and a different pair of ears, crossing her legs slowly and asking how his night is going. She says it warmly. She says it as if she had every right.

Sam glances up, and then he can't look away. Very long black hair. Gold at the tips, glowing. It isn't that she looks like the last one. It's that nothing about her looks different at all.
teases.wonder:
The last girl had the same. And the one before that. He's been telling himself it's a trend, some fashion in this world for dyed gold, or lantern-glow powder. But the eyes are the same lamp-gold too, and the warm bronze skin, and the faint sweetness of candle smoke clinging to her.

He's counting now. He didn't mean to start, but once you notice a pattern you can't un-notice it. Every one of them has appeared on a day when he'd been alone. Every one of them has vanished before he could get a straight answer.

She runs a finger lightly along his tie. "You're staring," she says, in a voice that is not quite hers and not quite someone else's. "Is something wrong?"

teases.title: Always the same
teases.text:
Sam has made a list. It's a short, embarrassing list: a fox, a cat, an elf, a dwarf. Each one a stranger, each with the same hair, the same eyes, the same warm bronze skin, and each one gone just before he-

He's staring at it when {alias} comes in, {form}, and reads it over his shoulder. "What's this?"

"A coincidence," he says, and she laughs, pressing herself against his back, her hands sliding around his waist. "Poor thing. You've been so frustrated."

choices.label: "You know exactly why."
choices.res: "Do I?" Her breath on his neck is hot enough to hurt. "Maybe I'm just a bad girl. Maybe you're just unlucky." She nips his ear. The door closes behind nobody.
choices.resIn: "You know exactly why." He feels her go quiet, very briefly, against his spine. Then her hands move again, as though it were all part of the plan.

choices.label: "Stay. Please."
choices.res: "Oh, I'd love to." She does, exactly until he's about to say something clever. Then he's alone with his list.
choices.resIn: "Stay. Please." She goes very soft at that. "Oh, I'd love to," she says, and turns his chair around so she can look at him properly.

teases.intro:
Sam has made a list. It's a short, embarrassing list, written on the back of an invoice with a pencil he keeps sharpening: a fox, a cat, an elf, a dwarf. Four columns: hair, eyes, skin, smell. Every line says the same thing four times.

He's still staring at it when the door opens without a knock. {alias} walks in as if she lived here, {form}, and drifts around the desk. She reads the list over his shoulder, and he feels her chin settle on it, smoke and warmth against his neck.

"What's this?" she asks lightly. "Homework?"
teases.wonder:
"A coincidence," he says, and she laughs, a low, delighted sound. It is the same laugh. Of course it is. He just never noticed, because the ears were different.

His pencil is shaking. Four girls, no, five now. All of them arrive with no warning and leave the same way. All of them stop, always, always, just before he can-

She's pressed up against his back now, hands sliding around his waist, her mouth near his ear. "Poor thing," {alias} murmurs. "You've been so frustrated. Tell me about it."

teases.title: Questions

image.comp: a girl in a man's lap in an armchair, his hands on her wrists, her face close to his, a finger against his lips, teasing

teases.text:
Sam is done being teased in silence. When {alias} appears, {form}, slipping into his lap with an easy smile, he catches her wrists.

"Who are you?"

"{alias}. I told you." She wriggles. Her hips do something distracting. "Ask a better question."

"Why do you always leave before-"

"Ah." She presses a finger to his lips. "Wrong question too. Try again in a few lives." She kisses him instead of answering, very thoroughly, and he does not notice the 'lives' until much later.

choices.label: "Who are you?"
choices.res: "{alias}," she says, "I told you." It's the lightest voice she's used so far, and it hides something. She slips out of his hands like water, laughing. "Ask me again in a few lives."
choices.resIn: "{alias}. I told you." She seems almost fond. "Ask a better question, {sam}." Her hips shift in his lap, a slow and very effective argument.

choices.label: "Why do you always leave?"
choices.res: "Ah." She presses a finger to his lips. "Try again in a few lives." Then she's gone, and he is alone with the word 'lives', turning it over.
choices.resIn: "Wrong question," she says gently, and lays a finger across his lips. "Let me give you a better one." Her other hand slides slowly down his chest.

teases.intro:
Sam has had enough of being teased in silence. He has been up for three days working on a plan, and the plan is simple: the next time one of them shows up, he is going to hold on.

He is at his desk, pretending to read, when {alias} slips in. {form} again, hair like a curtain of night with gold at the ends, hips swaying. She doesn't bother with a greeting. She crosses the room, drops lightly into his lap, and starts to loosen his collar.

He catches her wrists. Not hard. Just enough. Her eyebrows go up, interested, and she doesn't pull away.
teases.wonder:
Her pulse is quick under his thumbs. That's something: she has a pulse, she's warm, she's here. Not a ghost, not a dream, not a figment of overwork. He has been making excuses for weeks and this is the first time he's had the evidence in his hands.

He has a dozen questions lined up. Who are you. What are you. Why me. Why do you always go before it matters. The longer he looks into those lamp-gold eyes, the more he thinks she already knows every one of them, and has the answers sitting ready.

She wriggles a little, and his thoughts scatter. "Ask," says {alias}, with a smile like a dare. "I'm listening."

teases.title: Smoke and candle
teases.text:
Sam can't stop thinking about the dream. Gold lanterns, hundreds of them. A woman, laughing. Every time he reaches for the details, they slide away. But when {alias} comes through the door, {form}, and he smells candle smoke, he knows exactly where he's smelled it before.

She tries to kiss him. He turns his head.

"What's wrong?" Her smile slips for a heartbeat. "You're being strange."

"You smell like lanterns," he says.

choices.label: Hold her wrists, gently
choices.res: "Sam." Her voice is small. "Not yet." She presses her forehead against his chest for three long breaths. Then she's gone, and for the first time, he thinks she wanted to stay.
choices.resIn: He takes her wrists, gently, and holds on. She stills at once, and he can feel her heart beating through his fingers, quick and shy. "Sam," she says, much too softly.

choices.label: Pull her in and ask again
choices.res: "Don't." She kisses him to stop him, and it's a worse kiss, more frightened. She slips away. He is nearly sure now.
choices.resIn: He draws her in and asks again, quietly. Her breath catches. "Don't," she whispers, and presses her mouth to his, as if to stop the question where it stands.

teases.intro:
Sam can't stop thinking about the dream. Gold lanterns, hundreds of them, rising against a violet sky. A woman laughing, somewhere just out of reach. Every time he reaches for the details they slide away like fish. He has been absent-minded all day, losing track of conversations, staring at the flames in the hall.

That's why he catches the smell first. Candle smoke, warm and sweet, at his shoulder before the door has even finished opening. {alias} comes in, {form}, all long black hair and gold tips, and the dream rushes back so hard he has to put a hand on the wall.

She crosses to him, smiling, and leans in for a kiss. He turns his head, and her mouth lands on his cheek.
teases.wonder:
Lanterns. That's the thing he knows now. The smell, the gold, the way the light follows her as if it belongs to her. It isn't hair dye and it isn't a trick. Whoever she is, she is the woman from the dream, and every single girl before her was her too.

He feels oddly calm. The questions he'd been rehearsing have fallen away, and what's left is a quiet certainty, and a name rising from somewhere under his ribs. Not yet. He can almost taste it.

"What's wrong?" {alias} asks, and her smile slips for a heartbeat. "You're being strange." He looks at her, really looks, at the eyes like flame behind glass. "You smell like lanterns," he says.

teases.title: Another one
teases.text: {alias}, {form}, is already sitting on the stairs when Sam comes up, ankles crossed, glowing faintly. "You're late." She pulls him down beside her and kisses him, a warm lazy kiss, one hand tucked inside his shirt. "Didn't you miss me?" She's gone before he's finished deciding, leaving him with the gold hair on his sleeve and an uneasy thought.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." His voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and he thinks he hears a laugh.
choices.resIn: "Whoever you are-" he begins, and she kisses the rest of it away, slow and lazy and warm, one hand slipping inside his shirt.

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: He holds a long black hair up to the lamp. Gold at the tip. Exactly like all the others.
choices.resIn: He smiles and says nothing, which she plainly takes as encouragement. Her fingers play along his ribs.

teases.intro:
The upper landing is dark and smells of lamp oil, and Sam, coming up with a tray of clean glasses, nearly walks into someone's crossed ankles. {alias} is sitting on the top stair, {form}, glowing faintly in the gloom, black hair coiled around her like a sleeping cat, gold at the tips. Her eyes catch the single lamp below and hold it.

"You're late," she says, as though they'd made plans. She pulls him down beside her by the sleeve, the glasses chiming in his hands, and tucks herself against his side with the unhurried comfort of someone who's done this before.
teases.wonder:
Different ears, different name, same everything. He doesn't even have to count anymore. The hair, the eyes, the faint candle sweetness in the air: a signature, more than a disguise.

She watches him work it out, a little smile tucked into the corner of her mouth, as if daring him to say it aloud. "Didn't you miss me?" she asks, and her hand finds its way inside his shirt.

teases.title: Her eyes, again
teases.text:
Sam finds himself watching a girl's eyes: {alias}, {form}, who has appeared, as they always do, in the middle of a quiet hour. Glowing gold. She catches him at it and her smile deepens. She walks him to the wall, slow, and he lets her. "Looking for something?" she asks, and her hand slips into his waistband.

He doesn't get to answer.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." His voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and he thinks he hears a laugh.
choices.resIn: He tries to ask, and she answers by pulling him close, her hand slipping lower. "Not yet, {sam}," she says, and the name lands strangely.

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: Gold. Always the same gold. He is counting now.
choices.resIn: He smiles and says nothing, watching her eyes. Hers narrow, pleased, and she crowds closer.

teases.intro:
It's a quiet hour, the house humming low, the kind of lull in which Sam usually restocks shelves and thinks about nothing. Today he's thinking about gold. He's straightening a row of lamp oil tins when he feels it: that prickle at the back of the neck of being watched.

{alias} is leaning in the doorway, {form}, arms folded, a spill of black hair reaching past her hips and glowing at the ends. Her eyes are lamp-gold, warm and glowing and amused. She's caught him staring, he realizes; he's been staring at nothing for a full minute, waiting for her. She strolls over, slow, and he lets her walk him back against the wall.
teases.wonder:
Gold. Always the same gold, with the same slow glow at the edges, like a lamp seen through a windowpane. Five girls, six, and one pair of eyes. He has stopped telling himself it's a coincidence. He has started wondering what, exactly, he is supposed to do with the knowledge.

Her hand settles at his waist. "Looking for something?" asks {alias}, quietly, and he gets the strangest feeling that she wants him to answer honestly. That she would be pleased if he did.

teases.title: Different ears, same girl
teases.text: {alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the same everything else. She walks around him in a slow circle, trailing a hand across his shoulders. "What do you think? Do I suit it?" He thinks he's on to her. He thinks he's missing something, too. By the time he can say any of it, the chair beside him is empty.

choices.label: Call after her
choices.res: "Whoever you are..." His voice carries down the empty hall. No answer. But the candles flicker, and he thinks he hears a laugh.
choices.resIn: "Whoever you are-" he begins, and a hand slides over his mouth. "Hush," she whispers. "Let's not spoil it."

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.res: He sits there for a minute, then goes and checks the mirror in the hall. Nothing in it but him.
choices.resIn: He smiles, saying nothing, and she circles round to face him and settles in his lap, a thoughtful look in her lamp-gold eyes.

teases.intro:
{alias} has new ears today, {form}, and the same everything else. Sam finds her in the middle of the sitting room, turning on one heel to model them, as though he'd asked. Soft ears, a swish of tail, and underneath it all the same long black hair, the same gold at the tips swinging as she moves.

She walks a slow circle around his chair, trailing a fingertip over his shoulders as she goes, and the smell of candle smoke follows her like a cloak. "What do you think?" she asks. "Do I suit it?"
teases.wonder:
He thinks he's on to her. He thinks he's missing something, too: some detail so obvious that it keeps hiding in plain sight. The ears are charming. The girl under them is the same girl he's been losing for weeks, and he's almost sure that if he asks the right question, in the right voice, she'll answer.

She stops behind him and rests her chin on top of his head. "You're quiet," says {alias}, warm and curious. "Dangerous. Out with it."

teases.title: Say my name

image.comp: a girl in a man's lap, arms around his neck, forehead to his, a startled and delighted look, candles flaring around them
image.setting: Sam's bedroom at night, every candle burning gold

teases.text:
She comes to him as {alias} tonight, {form}, with a smile that is a little too wide. She sits in his lap, loops her arms around his neck, and he lets her. He lets her all the way to the edge of the kiss.

Then he says, quietly, "{goddess}."

Everything stops. Her smile stays where it is; her eyes don't. The candles dip. He doesn't know where the name came from: a dream of paper lanterns, a woman swinging in the dark, a promise about a debt. It was just there on his tongue.

"...Well," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore. "That took you long enough."

choices.label: "You've been teasing me for years."
choices.res: "Lives," she corrects, and kisses him, laughing and furious and relieved, all at once. "You remembered. You actually remembered. Don't stop." She stays a good long while this time.
choices.resIn: Everything stops. Her smile stays where it is; her eyes don't. Then she kisses him, hard and fast, as if to catch the name before it escapes, and starts working at his collar.

choices.label: "Why the disguises?"
choices.res: "Because the game is more fun when you don't know the rules." She presses her forehead to his. "And because I was afraid you'd say no, once you knew. Foolish of me." The glow around her brightens, a little shy.
choices.resIn: Her breath catches. For the first time, she doesn't have a quick answer. "Later," she says, in a voice that isn't {alias}'s anymore, and kisses him so he can't ask again.

teases.intro:
She comes to him as {alias} tonight, {form}, with a smile that is a little too wide. Sam is on the roof of the house, where he goes when the noise gets to be too much, and the lanterns hang below him like a field of tiny gold stars.

She doesn't knock; there's nothing to knock on. She just steps out of the dark, trailing candle smoke, sits in his lap and loops her arms around his neck. Her hair falls over them both, black and endless, the tips glowing in the dark.

He lets her. He lets her all the way to the edge of the kiss.
teases.wonder:
The thing about the dream is that it isn't a dream. It's a memory. Gold lanterns, a swing hung from nothing, a woman laughing at him in the dark. A promise about a debt, a door he'd walked through, and a voice that said: I'll find you.

Every girl was her. He knows it the way he knows his own name. The hair, the eyes, the smoke, the warm bronze skin, the laugh that keeps getting away from her. Every time he got close she slipped out of his hands.

Her lips hover an inch from his, patient and sure. It is the name he's been missing all along, and it is right there, heavy as a stone in his mouth. He says it, quietly, against her lips. "{goddess}."

teases.title: New rules

image.comp: a girl straddling a man on a bed, hands on his chest, a wicked smile, looking down at him

teases.text:
{goddess} arrives as {alias} tonight, {form}, hands on her hips, with the air of someone about to read terms and conditions.

"So you know. Which is a nuisance, because the disguises are fun and I'm not giving them up." She walks around him in a slow circle. "New rules. I come as someone new. You can play along, or you can call me by my name and I'll punish you. Either way, you don't finish. That part doesn't change."

"Is that a rule or a punishment?"

"Yes."

choices.label: Play along
choices.res: "Good," says {alias}, with a slow, wicked smile, settling into his lap as if she'd been introduced for the first time. The game is terrible, and wonderful.
choices.resIn: He plays along, and she brightens like a lamp being lit. "Good," says {alias}. "Then let's begin. Hello, stranger." She slides into his lap.

choices.label: "Nice to meet you, {goddess}."
choices.res: "Oh, you're going to pay for that." She pushes him back onto the bed and makes him, thoroughly, until he's begging. She never gives him what he's begging for.
choices.resIn: "Nice to meet you, {goddess}," he says politely, and watches her eyes narrow with a wicked light. "Oh, you will pay for that," she promises, and takes hold of his tie.

teases.intro:
The office is dim, and Sam is expecting trouble. He has been expecting it since the roof; every footfall in the hall is a possible goddess. When the door opens, he doesn't even look up.

"Good evening." {alias}, {form}, standing with her hands on her hips, hair swinging to her knees, gold tips glowing, eyes bright with mischief. She has the air of someone about to read out terms and conditions. {goddess} has dressed for the occasion in someone else's face.

"So you know," she says, walking a slow circle around his chair. "Which is a nuisance, because I like the disguises and I'm not giving them up."
teases.wonder:
She's enjoying this enormously. He can tell, because she can't quite keep her mouth straight, and because she keeps rolling the new name around in her mouth as though it were a sweet.

He knows exactly who is under the ears. Knowing changes things. It means that when she looks at him like that, there is a person behind the look, someone who has been waiting an awfully long time. It also means that he's in a great deal of trouble.

"New rules," she announces, and perches on the edge of the desk. "I come as someone new. You can play along, or you can call me by my real name, and I'll punish you. Either way, you don't finish. That part doesn't change." He raises an eyebrow. "Is that a rule or a punishment?"

"Yes."

teases.title: Introductions
teases.text:
{alias}, {form}, knocks on the office door and waits to be asked in, an act which is not at all like her.

"Good evening. I'm new in town." She holds out a hand, perfectly innocent. "I heard the owner could use some help." Her eyes are glowing gold and entirely innocent. Her hand is already inside his coat.

"You haven't introduced yourself," Sam says, and she gives him a look that says play along or suffer.

choices.label: "Welcome. What can you do?"
choices.res: "Oh," says the stranger, "a great many things." She shows him a few. All of them. None to completion. He is going to be walking funny for a while.
choices.resIn: "Oh," says the stranger, brightening, "a great many things." She closes the office door with her heel and does not look at all innocent.

choices.label: "{goddess}, you're a terrible actress."
choices.res: "I'm a wonderful actress and you are a spoilsport." She taps his nose, scandalized. "I'll have to teach you manners." By the end of the night, he is the one who has learned a lesson.
choices.resIn: "I'm a wonderful actress and you are a spoilsport," says the stranger, offended, and shows him exactly how she means to make it up to him.

teases.intro:
{alias}, {form}, knocks on the office door and waits to be asked in, an act which is not at all like her. Sam, who has been at the ledgers for hours, looks up with his pen halfway through a sum.

"Good evening." She comes in with small, careful steps, hands clasped, eyes cast down. Long black hair, gold-tipped, drifting around her like smoke. "I'm new in town. I heard the owner could use some help."

She offers him a hand, perfectly innocent. He takes it. Her other hand, he notes, is already inside his coat.
teases.wonder:
This is the part he used to dread: the strange woman, the warm smile, the sinking feeling that he'd been caught in a trap. Now he knows exactly whose trap it is. He knows the shape of the eyes under the lowered lashes. He knows the laugh she's swallowing.

It's ridiculous, and it's oddly sweet. She has been a stranger so many times that she has turned it into an art form, and tonight, she's decided to let him see the seams.

He wonders how long she can keep it up, and how far she'll go before the mask cracks. Whether, this time, she might let him finish. She looks up at him with huge, solemn gold eyes, wholly innocent. "You haven't introduced yourself, sir," says the stranger.

teases.title: Wrong pretext

image.comp: a girl wearing glasses and carrying a stack of books, leaning over a man seated at a desk, her hand on his shoulder, playful smile

teases.text:
The knock on the door is very polite. {alias} is standing outside in {form}, carrying a stack of books, wearing a pair of spectacles she definitely doesn't need.

"Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson." She's trying very hard not to laugh. "I understand it's... hands-on."

She is not subtle. He does not mind. Forty minutes of 'lessons' later, he's learned that a goddess in spectacles is considerably more dangerous than one without, and that she has no intention of giving him the final exam.

choices.label: Insist on a retake
choices.res: "No retakes," she says, smugly, tying her hair back. "Fail, learn, repeat." She kisses his forehead on the way out, which is somehow the worst part.
choices.resIn: "A retake? Already?" She sets down the book, eyes dancing. "Very well. Let's see what you remember."

choices.label: Beg for extra credit
choices.res: "Begging. Good start." She's glowing with satisfaction. She doesn't award extra credit.
choices.resIn: "Extra credit?" She taps her chin as if it's a serious question. "That depends. How badly do you want it?"

teases.intro:
The knock on the door is very polite. Sam has been waiting for it, in a way; there was a note on his desk this morning in handwriting he didn't recognise, saying only: "Lessons, seven o'clock." He has been trying not to wonder.

{alias} is standing outside in {form}, with a stack of books clutched to her chest and a pair of spectacles on her nose that she definitely doesn't need. Her hair is bound in a single tidy braid, and the gold tip swings as she nods. "Mr. {sam}? I'm here about the private lesson." She's trying very hard not to laugh. "I understand it's... hands-on."
teases.wonder:
He knows who she is. He knows, and she knows he knows, and they are both going to pretend very seriously that neither of them does. Somewhere in the back of his mind, a very small voice points out that this is absurd.

The spectacles slide down her nose, and she pushes them back with one finger, solemn as a clerk. A goddess of unknown age, in a pair of borrowed glasses, trying to look as if she's never seen a man before. It is probably the most ridiculous thing he's ever witnessed, and he can't stop smiling.

She opens a book at random and holds it up between them. "I'll start with a review," says {alias}, peeking over the top. "Unless you'd rather skip to the practical?"

teases.title: A new face, an old game
teases.text: Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across his desk and pretending very hard that they haven't met. "I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she says, as her foot slides up the inside of his thigh. He plays along. She's very good. She's also absolutely merciless, and leaves him exactly one breath from the edge.

choices.resIn: "{goddess}," he says, mildly. Her toes stop, and her grin breaks wide. "Spoilsport," she murmurs, delighted, and slides off the desk into his lap.

choices.label: Stay in character
choices.res: "Until next time," she says. "Remember my name." She leaves it unsaid, which is part of the game.
choices.resIn: "We've never met," he agrees solemnly. She makes a pleased little noise, and the foot travels higher.

teases.intro:
Tonight she's {alias}, {form}, lounging across his desk and pretending very hard that they haven't met. She has pushed the ledger aside to make room, black hair spilling over the pages in a shining river, the gold tips lighting the blotted figures from below. Her eyes are bright, and dancing, and perfectly innocent.

"I'm sure I'd remember a man like you," she says, with a perfectly straight face, as a bare foot slides slowly along the arm of his chair. "Have we done business before?"
teases.wonder:
He plays along, because it's easier than arguing and because he is curious how long she can hold the straight face. Not long, from the look of it: the corner of her mouth keeps betraying her. Every time he almost laughs, she nudges him with a toe.

He wonders whether tonight is the night she'll let him finish. He doubts it. Her toes are very warm and entirely too confident, and the look in her eyes says she has a plan. He just has to decide whether to give her the satisfaction of her name.

teases.title: Pick a name
teases.text:
{alias}, {form}, is waiting in the hall. "Guess," she says, and wraps herself around him. "Go on. I'll give you a point for every correct answer." He guesses 'Seliora' on the first try. She gives him a point. The point is one very pointed kiss.

The game goes on a good deal longer than he'd like. It ends the usual way.
